what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Small countries should build service plumbing, not chase GPUs
sections.para: Written for people from Romania and Portugal: the race for the biggest model, most GPUs and largest data centre is a commodity race a small country cannot win. The opportunity is the plumbing a talented person needs to sell services abroad, built once by the state, open source, with small models for every language.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Skip the capital race and commoditise the plumbing instead
sections.para: Frontier models and data centres are commodities a small country cannot catch. What stops talent selling abroad is company formation, cross-border hiring, payments, language, contracts and tax, which should be state infrastructure, as Estonia shows. It must be open source, demand for alternatives must exist early, and small models per language are the market.

sections.label: The event, and the word for what I mean
sections.line: The task for a small country is to facilitate
sections.para: At an event with Romanians, an embassy official said an embassy's job is to facilitate. SGraph Send's growth role, the Ambassador, was written the same way: create the conditions for organic growth. The question is what those conditions are for a small country in the age of agents, building on earlier arguments about Europe.

sections.label: The race you cannot win, and should not enter
sections.line: The frontier race is commodity territory for small players
sections.para: Biggest model, most GPUs, largest data centre all sit at the commodity end of a Wardley map, led by firms whose investment a small country's budget cannot match. Unless already an established open-model lab like Mistral, a country will not compete at the frontier and should look at the rest of the map.

sections.label: The opportunity is the plumbing
sections.line: Logistics, not talent, stops small-country services selling abroad
sections.para: A talented person in Cluj or Porto needs a company, cross-border contracts, payments, language and tax forms, each custom built and costly, with overhead falling on the buyer. In 2021, 18.5% of EU enterprises sold online at home, 8.1% to other EU countries and 4.6% beyond. Attrition, not talent, stops commerce.

sections.label: Infrastructure is the state's job
sections.line: Service plumbing is infrastructure the state should build once
sections.para: Like roads, company formation, cross-border hiring, payments, language and contracts should be built once with pooled money. Estonia did it: more than 142,000 e-residents, more than 43,000 companies, over 4,200 founded in 2026 by mid-September, all on X-Road, open source under MIT and shared with Finland and Iceland.

sections.label: Why it has to be open source
sections.line: No sovereignty without open source and open schemas
sections.para: A plumbing service owned by one vendor is lock-in with tarmac. Sovereignty means being able to leave, run a parallel service and move the data, which needs open code and schemas. What the public pays for should belong to the commons, so local firms can grow around it; sgit and vaults show the data-sovereignty piece.

sections.label: Create the demand before the day you need it
sections.line: Buy the alternative before the day you need it
sections.para: If a hyperscaler, payment provider or model API vanished, most European organisations would have nowhere to go, because markets for alternatives do not appear overnight. Run parallel services and buy local or open options now, accepting fewer features. Procurement is a lever the state already holds, and the case is resilience, not ideology.

sections.label: Smaller models, more of them
sections.line: Small models for each language and culture beat frontier
sections.para: Agents should use the least agency that does the job, and frontier models are too costly and powerful for daily work. The genesis market is small models per language and culture, such as each variety of Portuguese. Portugal's Amalia, released 1 July 2026 with 5.5 million euros of EU money, is open: a public road.

sections.label: Constraints are the input
sections.line: DeepSeek showed constraints produce innovation, not just excuses
sections.para: The GPU race only benefits those already in it. DeepSeek's V3 was trained in 2.788 million GPU hours on export-restricted H800 chips, with custom code around the throttled interconnect. Wardley describes China's directed investment and industrialisation; Europe should copy the mechanics with its own values, measuring results in lives, not parameters.

sections.label: What I learned spending millions on a distributed workforce
sections.line: Distributed talent works when the infrastructure comes first
sections.para: As a CISO and CTO the author spent millions on Upwork, building project management, structure and onboarding teams first, and hired talent as good as or better than usual. Infrastructure separates a working talent market from a race to the bottom, and lets jobs live outside capitals. Romania's tech sector is near 8% of GDP.

sections.label: The playbook
sections.line: Five moves: map, commoditise, create demand, invest, regulate
sections.para: Map where commerce stops between a talented person and a foreign buyer. Commoditise that plumbing as open roads. Create demand by buying alternatives early. Put money into genesis markets like small language models, not GPUs. Regulate once a layer has settled, then map again. Each move uses the larger players' weight.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A map from experience, not a national strategy
sections.para: The figures are the latest found and some are old: Eurostat's cross-border share is for 2021, Estonian counts come from the dashboard and press, Romanian figures from a 2025 report. The DeepSeek point is about constraint, not its disputed cost. The Upwork figures are unverifiable, and Estonia's details may not transfer.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: a voice memo, earlier essays and cited figures
sections.para: The piece comes from Dinis Cruz's voice memo of 12 October 2026 and builds on Europe's strategic opportunity in GenAI, the open-source sovereign cloud essay and two pieces on Portugal. Figures come from Eurostat, the e-Residency dashboard, RIA on X-Road, Reuters on Amalia, the DeepSeek V3 report, Business Forum and Simon Wardley.
